I have been ordering shawarma wraps from this restaurant for years, and unfortunately, my experience today was quite disappointing.
While having my shawarma wrap prepared, I asked the employee to add some donair sauce. Her immediate response was that I would have to pay extra for it. I explained that I have been getting shawarma wraps from this restaurant for years and have never been charged for adding a small amount of sauce to my wrap. I was still willing to pay, so I agreed.
However, I was surprised to see a $2 charge for what was essentially just a squeeze of donair sauce. I understand that businesses have costs and policies, but charging $2 for such a small amount of sauce—especially when this was never an additional charge in my previous visits—felt unreasonable and disappointing.
I hope the management can reconsider this policy and be more transparent about additional charges. I have been a long-time customer, and I would expect a better experience and a little more consideration for returning customers.

Notes: To begin with, this is easily one of the cleanest shawarma spots I’ve been to. The seating area is well kept and comfortable enough to sit down with a laptop, which is pretty rare for shawarma places. The whole space feels calm, organized, and just nice to be in.
They’ve got a wide variety of dishes and clearly keep up with trends, things like quinoa bowls, kunafa chocolate, and lighter, healthier options. One thing that stood out is that they sell their own in-house spice blends (nutmeg spices) under their own brand, which is a nice touch. I also got a chance to see the kitchen, and it was very clean, well kept, and nicely organized.
Portion sizes are generous, and the food feels healthy but filling. Their thick rice is kind of their signature in the shawarma bowls , it’s hearty and easily fills you up for the whole day. Overall, it’s a solid spot if you want something clean, reliable, and a bit more modern than your usual shawarma joint.

POI: Using in house bread and a tawa for shawarmas would take this to the next level. Offering more authentic shawarma topping options for Mediterranean customers and focusing on crispier wraps would really elevate the overall shawarma experience.

I just wanna start off by saying I love Mezza so much. I am there at the Barrington location probably once a week if not more it is my go to spot when I’m in Halifax today I was out of the city going to Hubbards so I stopped at the Tantallon location… All I have to say was this location is nothing like the others I’ve been to. The service was terrible. The workers were disengaged and rude to say the least to the customers. They didn’t have any chicken ready we had to wait almost 20 minutes for  Not even half of a bucket of chicken to be brought out for five customers which resulted in all of the customers waiting to be served to have less than three scoops of chicken on our bowls and Shawarma plates. This is unfortunate as I know what the standards are as I go to Barrington Street practically every week and it is always so good and consistent at the other locations. I was just disappointed because I was so excited to come and have Mezza on my way out to Hubbard’s this evening, and I was very, very, very disappointed with the overall atmosphere & service and quality of the food. Not to mention it didn’t help having staff who were completely dismissive and looked like they didn’t want to be serving a rush of customers at dinner time. I initially visited Mezza during their opening week a few years ago, and admittedly, I wasn't really impressed with my meal and swore to never return.

I decided it was time to give them another chance. Mezza is a fast food type Lebanese restaurant chain established in Halifax and has since grown to have many locations across the maritimes.

The building boasts modern, minimalistic exterior decor, and the same can be said for the interior. While it may be minimalist, it exudes luxury and class by utilizing premium materials such as wood, polished concrete, and glass.

The interior features a dining room with individual tables and chairs, along with a countertop checkout area. The checkout area is akin to those of a sandwich shop. You order, and as your food is being made, you are asked if you want certain toppings or sauces.

Due to utilizing this kind of assembly business model, it allows them to assemble the meal efficiently. I ordered two protein bowls, and it took less than 10 minutes overall for me to order and leave with the food. Additionally, this location features a drivethru.

The service I received was excellent and courteous. The store was extremely clean and well lit with a mixture of natural and artificial light.

Overall, the food was delicious and filling, and the service I received was good.

(Translated by Google) Nothing to write home about, the chicken mixture was really poor quality; you could taste the chicken skin and lots of tendons. In short, I was expecting at least some meat. You need to regulate the temperature on your spits, otherwise the meat cooks too quickly and the fat burns. The tabbouleh is too parsley-laden for my taste... The recipe needs revising. You need to add MORE bulgur! It's too green for tabbouleh, unfortunately. The fries are way too salty. It's not good because it makes you thirsty with every bite. The bread... I expected better for Lebanese... Well, yes... It's mass-produced... The bread was too dry once folded; even with my strong molars, I couldn't chew it. The vegetables were alright; it was nice to have real chili peppers. The falafels were very mealy but had a good flavor. Otherwise, the atmosphere was nice. The concept boasts about being very family-oriented, but it strays too far from that and becomes inconsistent. It's too close to the kind of fast food you eat in your car between noon and 2 pm. They should avoid using family photos in this case because it gives a bad impression considering the quality of the food.

And since shawarma is twice the price as anywhere else I’ve had it I just make my own. Here is how it’s done!  Buy a rotisserie chicken from Costco for $7.99, 5 pack of pita for $3 (make sure it’s fresh - soft), a large container of extra strong garlic sauce for $6.99 from Mama, a jar of home made pickled turnips at the local Moncton market for $11 (expensive but they are perfect) and a spice mix from Cyprus €2 (see photo - I just ordered another 8 packs 🤣) All of this cost me around $36! That’s two small wraps from Mezza. I can make 6-8 big wraps from one chicken (depending on what’s available at the time of purchase at Costco) - and still have loads of everything else left over for my next chicken!! The trick is to shred the chicken and crisp it up in a hot pan with the mixed spices! It’s so good! Try this out - you’ll never go to Mezza again 🤣🤣🤣

My girlfriend Caroline has had the food from Mezza before, although for me it was a first. But I haven’t found good Greek food on the island, so I was very hopeful when I saw souvlaki and Greek salad on the menu, so when I showed Caroline the menu, she picked Wednesday evening for our supper date. The restaurant interior looked new, clean and well staffed, with a long line up as it was just past five pm.

I knew I wanted souvlaki but they have such a large menu that I could eat there for a week without repeating myself too often. ;)

I ordered the Mixed Grill, some stuffed grape vine leaves, and of course baklava for desert. The chicken souvlaki, while tasty was not the best I’ve had, in fact I found it a touch dry and rubbery so I’m not sure how they marinade it. Typically it’s garlic, rosemary, oregano lemon juice, olive oil, wine, and refrigerated for a lengthy amount of time to let those flavours soak in. These were disappointing in texture and flavour, I’d give them 2.5 out of 5. Okay, but I found I enjoyed the chicken shawarma meat and the donair quite a bit more. They were served with a side of donair sauce and a garlic mayo that  I hope they weren’t calling tzatziki sauce, as the closest it’s ever been to yoghurt was while stored in the refrigerator, but as a condiment for the chicken shawarma it was lovely. Their hummus was good, and I enjoyed the pickled turnip. We both opted for rice, which was alright.
